title: Moderator erasure by user ID may leave the user's name in recent subscribers while reporting success
current: When the moderator erase form resolves a user ID (directly, or by looking up a username), the route calls untrackSubscriberById only and shows 'erase success'. The username-based recent-subscriber cleanup (eraseFromRecentSubscribers) runs only on the partial-erase branch. Self-erasure, by contrast, calls both.
evidence: untrackSubscriberById calls eraseSubscriberOrdersById (order records by user ID) and clears subscriber stats. Recent-subscriber display fields are indexed by username in recentSubscriberPostsByUsernameKey and are removed by eraseFromRecentSubscribers, which this branch never calls. Whether eraseSubscriberOrdersById also clears those display fields is unverified.
assumptions: That eraseSubscriberOrdersById does not already remove the username-indexed display fields.
investigate: Does eraseSubscriberOrdersById (src/server/data/recentSubscriberErasure.ts:29) remove the recent-subscriber display entry and the by-username index?
Test: subscribe as a user, erase them by user ID from the moderator form, then read every post's recent-subscriber fields.
required: The erase-success toast only after every store that holds the user's data is cleared; otherwise the partial toast.
tests: Moderator erase by user ID removes the username from recent subscribers and the by-username index.

criticality.why: A privacy erasure reported as complete could leave the user's name visible on goal posts.
